name: Hanalani Schools Holiday Craft Fair
schedule_text: Saturday, November 14, 2026, 9 AM-2 PM.
admission: Free
description: Central Oʻahu school craft and food fair, free to shoppers.
source_label: LocalHawaiiEvents.com craft fairs guide (third-party, checked 2026-10-06)
notes: A KITV roundup showed Hanalani also ran a Spring Craft Fair on April 25, 2026 with 60+ crafters and food vendors. No 2027 spring date found yet. Different from the Mililani Town Association Holiday Craft Fair on your skip list.

name: HUOA Winter Craft and Gift Fair
schedule_text: Saturday, November 28, 2026; one listing also shows a second day on Sunday, November 29. Hours not stated.
description: Annual cultural craft and gift fair bringing together the Okinawan community and craft shoppers in Waipahu each November.
source_label: VendorsMap Waipahu listings (third-party)
notes: The source lists Nov 28-29 in one entry and Nov 28 only in another. I included only the date both entries share. Food vendors are not confirmed. Check HUOA's own page.

name: McKinley High School Band & Orchestra Winter Craft & Gift Fair
schedule_text: Annual, held on a Sunday in early December, 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. The 2025 edition was Sun Dec 7. The 2026 date is not confirmed.
organizer: McKinley High School Band & Orchestra (Band Boosters)
description: Band and orchestra fundraiser. Every booth fee goes to the McKinley Band & Orchestra programs. The organizer page has separate food-vendor and general vendor applications and vendor sections: lawn and makai, cafeteria, auditorium parking lot, and library lanai.
source_label: Organizer page (McKinley HS Band & Orchestra, Google Sites); KHON2 (Dec 2024)
notes: The organizer page I could read shows the Dec 7, 2025 edition, not a 2026 one, so confidence stays medium and no 2026 date is listed. Past editions: Dec 3, 2023, Dec 8, 2024 and Dec 7, 2025 (organizer page and event listings), all 9-2. KHON2 (Dec 2024) called it the largest in the fair's 40+ year history and named Cindy Wong as event coordinator, and said KC Waffle Dog would be there. A third-party calendar lists it for December 2026 with the date still to be confirmed. Confirm the 2026 date with the organizer. Shopper admission not stated. Food vendors do appear (the organizer page offers a food vendor application).

name: Mililani High School Holiday Food & Craft Fair
schedule_text: Saturday, November 21, 2026, 9:00am–2:00pm. The organizer holds two Food & Craft Fairs each school year, in November and April.
description: Holiday food and craft fair benefiting MHS athletics. The organizer says it offers 220+ spots for food trucks, food pop-ups, crafters, artisans, retailers, and community and school groups.
source_label: Organizer's own website (vendor update blog) and organizer vendor page
notes: Organizer pages confirm the date and hours. The street address comes from a vendor's event listing (Donnie Ann Creations) for the April fair. Its organizer is MHSAF, a separate event from the Mililani Town Association's craft fairs (the MTA autumn fair is Sept 12 at Mililani Mauka Rec 5), so it is not a duplicate unless your skip list says otherwise. The Facebook and Instagram handle is as posted on the organizer's blog; the Facebook page itself was not opened. Admission is not stated for the November fair. The April shoppers page says parking is free. The vendor URL is the organizer's vendor-information page, not a confirmed application form. A third-party site (vendorsmap.com) repeats the Nov 21 9am–2pm listing.

name: Ahiki Acres produce pre-order pickup
schedule_text: Pre-order online; pickup Sundays 10:30 am-4:30 pm at ʻAi Love Nalo (pre-order required). Also at Kailua Town Farmers' Market Sundays 8 am-12 pm. The online marketplace is updated Thursday afternoons.
description: Small Native Hawaiian-owned vegetable farm in Waimānalo that sells weekly pre-ordered produce for pickup.
source_label: Organizer website
notes: This is a pre-order marketplace, not a fixed-share CSA; the farm ran a prepaid CSA in 2019. Sierra Club Oʻahu also lists farm pickup Fridays 12-2 pm and Waimānalo Co-Op and Health Center Wednesday pickups, but that is older third-party info. The Instagram handle is from a CTAHR farm profile listing Ahiki Acres.

name: Asagi Hatchery (fresh eggs and produce storefront)
schedule_text: The hatchery's own contact page lists store hours of Monday to Friday 8am-5pm and Saturday 9am-noon.
description: Family-owned hatchery in Kalihi hatching chicks since 1935. It sells hatching eggs, chicks, chicken supplies and feed, and fruit trees. Fresh eggs and produce for sale are not currently confirmed.
source_label: Business website contact page (undated)
notes: Primarily a hatchery and supply store, so it is a stretch as an egg stand. The home page address is 1830 Kanakanui Street, and the site shows a fruit-tree availability list dated 2026, so the website is maintained. It asks customers to call (808-845-4522) before visiting for trees. Contact-page hours are undated, and non-review directories give different hours (for example Mon-Fri 9-3), so confirm by phone. A hawaiianlocal.com listing, which seems to repeat the Facebook text, says it sold fresh eggs from Peterson Upland Farm; the user note says that farm closed in 2024 (Honolulu Magazine), so egg sourcing may have changed. The Facebook page is the business's own. An Instagram handle (@asagihatchery) appears on a farm-directory listing but was not seen on the business's own pages, so it is left null.

name: Da Banana Stand (Living Circle Farms Hawaii)
schedule_text: Open seasonally and by appointment only.
description: Seasonal produce and natural products grown on the farm and sold at Da Banana Stand.
source_label: Business's own website
notes: Page is undated. Appointment-only, so it may not be a walk-up roadside stand. No hours or contact method retrieved.

name: De La Mesa Farms CSA boxes
schedule_text: Historically CSA boxes with pickup locations on the Windward side and in Honolulu (listed in 2020). The farm has since relocated to Washington State.
description: Former Waimānalo farm (Bryan and Natalie Mesa) that sold microgreens, produce, salsa and CSA boxes on Oʻahu before moving to Tacoma, WA.
source_label: GoFarm Hawaii farmer profiles (Windward)
notes: No longer an Oʻahu operation, so likely not listable. GoFarm Hawaii's Windward profile lists De La Mesa Farms as 'online (re-located to WA)'. A Land Conservation Assistance Network entry says the owners began in Waimānalo and bought 2.5 acres in Tacoma in 2020, and the farm's own site (delamesafarms.com) and a South Sound Magazine feature describe a Tacoma farm and CSA. The Sierra Club Oʻahu list that supplied the original row is a pandemic-era resource page. The handle @delamesahawaii and the delamesahawaii.com website are tied to this farm by GoFarm Hawaii's 2018 farmer profile (website and Instagram/Facebook). The delamesahawaii.com site was not re-checked as live, and the handle may be dormant. A Forbes 2019 profile also describes an Oʻahu CSA and Kakaʻako/Kailua market booths, which are historical.

name: Eggs Hawaii / Ka Lei Eggs
venue_name: Eggs Hawaii Inc - Island Fresh Eggs (retail store)
organizer: Eggs Hawaii (Ka Lei Eggs / Hawaiian Maid Eggs)
description: Retail store of Eggs Hawaii selling Ka Lei and Hawaiian Maid island fresh eggs from the family farm in Waianae, in an industrial part of Kalihi.
source_label: Eggs Hawaii own contact page (store name, address, phone (808) 841-7695); Honolulu Magazine staff pick (older, pandemic-era)
notes: Own contact page (read in the first pass) names the store and address; unit is given as 1E in one place and E1 in another, so no unit is listed here. Phone (808) 841-7695; company office is 1590 Hau Street, (808) 841-7521. Honolulu Magazine (about 2020) gave 8:30-3:30 Mon-Fri and 7:30-2 Sat, and a local-eggs directory repeats those hours (closed Sundays, some holidays), but other directory listings show 7:30 weekday openings, and no current own page states hours, so schedule_text is null. No 2026 own post found, so still_active is null rather than true. Ka Lei eggs are also sold at Kakaʻako Farmers Market (already in the directory). Facebook handle not captured. Review sites not used.

name: Farm Link Hawaiʻi (local produce boxes, delivery and Kalihi hub pickup)
venue_name: Farm Link Kalihi Hub (food hub / warehouse)
schedule_text: Pickup at the Kalihi hub 10 am-3:30 pm, six days a week (Wed-Mon, closed Tuesday). Delivery windows 9 am-5 pm on most days, with next-day delivery when you check out by midnight.
admission: Free pickup with no order minimum; delivery has a $50 order minimum and an $11.99 fee, waived for Farm Link Members and EBT/SNAP households.
description: Online local-grocery aggregator that sources from Oʻahu farms, ranchers and bakers and delivers islandwide or offers hub pickup. Honolulu Magazine (2020) described a $30 CSA produce box assembled from its farms.
source_label: Organizer website
notes: The site says no subscription is required, so this is order-by-order rather than a fixed-box CSA. Whether the $30 CSA box still exists was not confirmed. The Kalihi street address was not stated in the pages I saw.

name: Frankie's Nursery Fruit Stand
schedule_text: Tuesday to Saturday, 9:00am to 3:00pm. Closed Sunday and Monday.
description: Fruit stand at a tropical fruit-tree nursery selling fruit harvested daily from mature trees plus homemade tropical juices. Fruit varies by season; the site gives mangoes as primarily a summer fruit and durians as a winter fruit. Visitors can walk the nursery grounds, where the fruit trees are for sale.
source_label: Frankie's Nursery official website
notes: Own page, but it carries no update date (footer shows 2022), so current hours should be confirmed. The site shows an Instagram link but no handle, so instagram is null.

name: Haleiwa Fruit Shack
schedule_text: Usually open daily, 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. The stand's own TikTok says it is open 7 days a week 'most of the time'. A TikTok post also says it sells at the KCC Farmers Market on Saturdays, 7:30–11:15 a.m.
description: Roadside fruit shack selling fruit platters, fresh-pressed sugarcane juice and cold coconuts.
source_label: Business Facebook page; hours from nateeatshawaii.com listing and the business's TikTok (@thehaleiwafruitshack)
notes: No Instagram handle was confirmed, so it is null. The TikTok handle is @thehaleiwafruitshack. The address is the same on the Facebook page and several listings, but one TikTok caption shows a different number (62-540), so verify. Hours may vary day to day.

name: Ho Farms produce pickup (Ewa Beach / Honolulu)
venue_name: Old Fort Weaver Road (Ewa Beach); Republik (Concert and Event Center) (Honolulu)
schedule_text: Per an undated Sierra Club Oʻahu list: pickup Mondays 3-5 pm on Old Fort Weaver Road (Ewa Beach) and Saturdays 1-3 pm at Republik (Concert and Event Center), Honolulu. Not confirmed as current.
description: Online-order produce pickup from Ho Farms, a family farm in Kahuku. The farm has also added fields in Ewa Beach.
source_label: Sierra Club Oʻahu Group, Island Resources (third-party list)
notes: I could not reach a current page on Ho Farms' own site showing these pickups. The same text appears in a Sierra Club blog that the search engine dated to about 2020, and it points to a Local Line ordering page (localline.ca/hofarms). It reads as a pandemic-era online-ordering list. The text does not say whether a subscription or box is offered. The farm's own X account lists hofarms.com as its website, which is the only own-source link I found. Ho Farms produce is also sold through Farm Link Hawaiʻi (a separate seller). Pickup sites are not verified as current, so still_active is null. Do not list until the farm confirms.

name: ʻĀINA Farm Stand
venue_name: Kōkua Learning Farm (Unit B on the highway, with Kōkua General Store)
schedule_text: Tuesday to Friday 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.; Saturday opens 8:30 a.m. (Saturday closing time not stated in the source).
description: Stand opened November 2024 in the property's historic flower shop. Sells produce from the Kōkua Learning Farm and other local farms plus value-added products. Proceeds go to the foundation.
source_label: Community article (Oahu Travel Guide), indexed about 4 days before 2026-10-31
notes: Third-party source; the organizer's own page was not retrieved. Haleʻiwa is outside the listed towns (Waiʻanae, Nanakuli, Kunia, Wahiawā, Waialua).

name: Kahuku Land Farms Stand
neighborhood: Kahuku (across from Kawela Bay, near Turtle Bay Resort)
schedule_text: <cite index="1-5,1-6">A 2017 Star-Advertiser piece places the stand on Kamehameha Highway, mauka side, across the Kawela Bay entrance, and says it is open daily during daylight hours.</cite> Not confirmed as current by any own page or organizer.
description: <cite index="1-9,1-10">A collective of roadside stands, loosely known as Kahuku Land Farms, selling bags of cut fruit and whole fruit.</cite> <cite index="1-11">Most of the produce is grown on farms just behind the stand, on land leased out by Turtle Bay Resort (as of 2017).</cite>
source_label: Honolulu Star-Advertiser, North Shore snapshot (2017)
notes: No own website, social account or organizer found. Street address left null: the 56-800 Kamehameha Hwy address on an aggregator is Kahuku Farms' address, and a map-app address and phone were not used because they come from map listings. Kuilima Farm's own site says its farm stand is mauka of the Ritz-Carlton Oʻahu, Turtle Bay, across from Kawela Bay (https://kuilimafarm.com/experience), so the two stand clusters may overlap, but nothing ties this collective to Kuilima. Fodor's describes the Kuilima Farm Stand as having multiple stalls. A Honolulu Magazine road trip (about Aug 2026) says the writers browsed neighboring stands next to Kuilima Farm Stand, which suggests roadside stands still operate there, but it does not name this collective. A Hawaiʻi Life guide (about Mar 2026) lists 'Kahuku Fruit Stands' open daily 9-5 and ties them to Kahuku Farms, which conflicts with the independent-stand description, so that schedule was not used. still_active is null: nearby stands appear to be operating but this collective is not confirmed. Duplicate of the next row; they should be merged in the directory.

name: Kahuku Land Farms Stand (Kahuku fruit stands)
schedule_text: A 2017 Star-Advertiser piece said open daily during daylight hours. Not confirmed as current.
description: <cite index="1-9">A collective loosely known as the Kahuku Land Farms stand, on Kamehameha Highway across from the Kawela Bay entrance.</cite> Sells cut fruit, whole fruit and coconuts per the 2017 article.
source_label: Honolulu Star-Advertiser, North Shore snapshot (2017)
notes: Duplicate of the previous row (same source, same findings); recommend listing once. No own page, organizer or social account found and no usable street address. Only the 2017 article describes this collective by name. Honolulu Magazine (about Aug 2026) mentions neighboring stands beside Kuilima Farm Stand, but the operator and current hours of this collective are unverified. The 9-5 daily schedule in the Hawaiʻi Life guide is attributed there to Kahuku Farms, so it was not used. Kuilima Farm Stand's own site lists 9am-5pm daily at 57-146 Kamehameha Hwy; it is a separate listing and was not merged.

name: Kahumana Organic Farms CSA
schedule_text: Weekly or bi-weekly half- or full-share produce box, with pickup or doorstep delivery chosen at signup (per Honolulu Magazine description of the site's ordering flow). Pickup locations around the island.
description: Certified organic 25-acre farm in Lualualei Valley offering CSA produce and meal boxes with island pickup sites, plus a Farm Hub fruit box sold through Oahu Fresh.
source_label: Organizer website
notes: Same organization as the existing Kahumana Organic Farms Farm Market entry; this is the CSA program. Current prices and pickup sites were not on the pages I saw. Slow Food Oahu (undated, roughly 2024) lists $30-$32 per box with 13 pickup sites. The site also advertises free summer Kaukau 4 Keiki produce boxes for eligible keiki, which is a separate program.

name: Kualoa Coconut Man
schedule_text: Daily, 9:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
description: Simple roadside stand on Kamehameha Highway selling fresh coconuts opened on the spot, plus fruit such as bananas and papaya.
source_label: FastFoodClub article, 6 Hawaii Roadside Stands (indexed about 31 days before this research)
notes: The article gives the location only as Kamehameha Highway in Kaneohe, with no street address or hours. A separate aggregator page garbles the address, so I left it null. Verify the exact location and hours before publishing.

name: Let's Grow Farms multi-farm CSA
schedule_text: Weekly bag of seasonal produce. Pickup Saturdays noon-4 pm at Keneke's Grill in Punaluʻu and Sundays 11 am-3 pm at the Waialua Farm Stand. The traditional 6-month prepaid CSA also lists pickup in Hawaiʻi Kai, at Mori by Art & Flea, on-farm in Pearl City, or home delivery.
description: Two-farmer CSA (Dave and Thanh) that grows and packs produce weekly and adds produce from other Oʻahu farms. Has a sliding-scale Food For All program.
source_label: Organizer website
notes: Price not on the pages I saw; Slow Food Oahu (undated, roughly 2024) says $20-$25 per bag. The site mentions Instagram and Facebook but gave no handles. Site footer shows Copyright 2026.

name: Local Hawaiian Produce weekly delivery bags
schedule_text: Weekly produce bag delivered on Fridays, with delivery on Oʻahu included.
organizer: Local Hawaiian Produce (Farmer Dave and family)
description: Family farm bagging produce from a Punaluʻu orchard, a Mokuleia organic farm and other trusted organic farmers for weekly delivery.
source_label: Organizer website
notes: Price not stated on the page I saw. Page is undated. The Let's Grow Farms site also names a Dave Burlew farming in Punaluʻu; the connection between the two is not confirmed.

name: Local Inside CSA (Hawaii Agricultural Foundation, HAF Ag Park Kunia)
venue_name: HAF Ag Park, Kunia (produce source); pickup sites around Oʻahu
schedule_text: No current schedule or pickup sites found. <cite index="78-2">Hawaii Magazine reports HAF launched the Local Inside CSA in 2015.</cite> That article is older.
description: <cite index="78-3">Older coverage says bags were filled with produce grown at the HAF Ag Park in Kunia by small farmers leasing land there.</cite> <cite index="81-1">GoFarm Hawaii says Local Inside, previously a CSA program, now serves as a platform connecting farmers with the community.</cite>
source_label: Hawaii Agricultural Foundation website (contact and farmers pages, ©2025); GoFarm Hawaii; Hawaii Magazine (older)
notes: HAF itself is active: its own site (©2025) describes the Ag Park at Kunia as supporting growers on Central Oʻahu and lists contact info (info@hawaiiagfoundation.org, (808) 927-9749, office at 3538 Waialae Ave #203, Honolulu; the office is not a pickup venue). <cite index="19-4">An HSTA article (about Oct 2026) says HAF is recruiting for its 2026-2027 teacher cohort.</cite> The retrieved HAF pages did not mention a Local Inside CSA bag or pickup program. Together with the GoFarm statement (about 2024) that Local Inside became a platform, the bag-and-pickup model may no longer run. Pickup sites are unverified, so side is null (the Ag Park is in Kunia, central Oʻahu, but pickups were elsewhere). kind is null because none of the allowed kinds fits a CSA. A LocalHarvest listing (old) gave small and large bag prices; those are not current and were not used. still_active is null: the organization is active but the CSA/pickup program is unconfirmed. Not suitable to list as a recurring pickup until HAF confirms.

name: Lohelani Farms CSA
schedule_text: Bi-weekly box of 8-10 items (salad and cooking greens, roots, herbs, seasonal fruit). Delivery for Central Oʻahu residents. Subscribe for one month (2 boxes) or two months (4 boxes).
admission: One month, 2 boxes, delivered to Central Oʻahu: $40. Two months, 4 boxes: $72.
description: Farm CSA delivering a bi-weekly produce box to Central Oʻahu; subscribers sign up by contacting the farm through its website.
source_label: Organizer website
notes: Page undated; I could not confirm current availability. The farm's location was not stated in the results.

name: Mahina Pua Farm CSA box
schedule_text: Produce is sold by CSA box, à la carte, or at farmers markets: Kakaʻako Wednesdays, Kaiser HS and Niu Valley Tuesdays, Āina Haina Sundays. CSA pickup times were not stated in the source I used.
description: Urban farm growing vegetables on the east side of Oʻahu and selling by CSA box, à la carte and at four farmers markets.
source_label: Organizer website
notes: I'm placing it on the east side based on a listing's 'East side of Oahu' wording; the farm address is not stated. Price and pickup details exist in a LocalHarvest listing, which I did not use. Check the farm's site for current terms.

name: MAʻO Organic Farms CSA
schedule_text: Weekly or every-other-week box with an 8-box commitment. Boxes are delivered to pickup sites across Oʻahu.
description: Organic produce CSA from the Waiʻanae farm and youth-training nonprofit; the 8-box agreement is described as making subscribers co-producers.
source_label: Organizer website
notes: The CSA page shows no price or pickup-site list. Older press (2020) cited $32 per box; Slow Food Oahu (roughly 2024) says $32 with 13 pickup sites. Page currency not confirmed.

name: Mohala Farms CSA
address: P.O. Box 204, Waialua, HI 96791 (mailing address only)
schedule_text: CSA: weekly bundles. Slow Food Oahu (undated, roughly 2024) reports Thursday baskets with pickup at the farm or in Moʻiliʻili, an annual fee of $25 and three-month subscriptions. The farm's own sign-up page lists Full ($25) and Half ($15) bundles and says new members depend on available supply. Separately, the farm sells every Saturday, 8:30am–12pm, at the Waialua Farmer's Co-op Market behind the Old Waialua Sugar Mill.
admission: Per Slow Food Oahu: $25 annual fee, 3-month subscriptions, small basket $20, large basket $30, customizable.
description: Nonprofit organic farm in Waialua selling produce through a CSA program and a Saturday farmers' market stall.
source_label: Organizer's own website (©2026 footer); CSA terms from Slow Food Oahu
notes: The farm's own current site confirms the CSA program, the Saturday Waialua market with times, and the phone 808-478-8469. It does not give a Thursday pickup day or the Moʻiliʻili pickup. Those details are still only from Slow Food Oahu (undated), and the CSA prices conflict between Slow Food and the sign-up page, so confirm with the farm before publishing. The Instagram profile @mohalafarms describes 'an organic farm located in Waialua, HI'. Its bio carries older market hours (Haleʻiwa market Thursdays, farm Saturdays 9–5) that contradict the website, so it may be stale. The Roots Program Kalihi Valley hub-partner list gives a different handle, mohala_farms, which I could not match to a live profile. The farm's own sign-up page shows the contact email mohalafarms@gmail.com. The contact page shows info@mohalafarms.org. The street address of the farm was not found in a first-party source; Manta shows 66-1380 Kaukonahua Rd but it is an unclaimed directory listing and was not used. Kind is left null because CSA is not in the allowed kinds. The farm's market stall is a vendor stall at the Waialua market, not its own market. The Facebook handle was not confirmed.

name: North Shore Farm Stand
address: Hale'iwa Road at Paalaa Rd, Haleiwa, HI 96712
schedule_text: Wednesdays 12pm to 6pm per the contact page; the homepage says Wednesdays and Thursdays 12pm to 6pm.
description: Stand selling fresh produce and products from North Shore farmers, homesteaders and entrepreneurs. Farmers listed include Tin Roof Ranch (fruit orchard, chickens, turkeys, sheep) and Ala Mai Farmstead.
source_label: Organizer website (home and contact pages)
notes: Home page says Wed and Thu 12-6pm; contact page lists Wednesdays only. Pages are undated (footer copyright 2024), so confirm hours with the stand. Address is Haleʻiwa but the stand serves the Waialua moku.

name: North Shore Farm Stand (Āina Sustainability Growers of Hawaii)
address: 66-249 Kamehameha Hwy Unit B, Haleiwa, HI 96712
schedule_text: The farm's own site says the stand is open to the public Wednesdays and Thursdays, 12 p.m. to 6 p.m. A Haleʻiwa Town guide lists different hours (Wed–Fri 9 a.m.–3 p.m., Sat 8:30 a.m.–2:30 p.m.), so verify before listing.
organizer: Āina Sustainability Growers of Hawaii LLC (owner and farmer Luis Dasilveira)
description: Farm stand in Haleʻiwa town selling fresh produce and products grown and made in Moku o Waialua.
source_label: Farm's own website; address and alternate hours from haleiwatown.com market guide
notes: The farm's page gives Wed/Thu 12–6 but carries no date. The street address and the conflicting hours come from haleiwatown.com, which calls it the ĀINA Farm Stand. I matched it to this website by name and town. Confirm the schedule with the farm.

name: Oahu Fresh (Farmers' Market Box / subscription delivery)
schedule_text: Subscription service with weekly or biweekly produce bag delivery or pickup at various island pickup locations; one member comment on the site mentions weekly Wednesday delivery. Order cutoffs apply each week.
admission: Farmers' Market Box $25 plus a delivery fee, per the company's shop page. A $15 membership fee is cited by Slow Food Oahu and older company pages, not on the current shop page seen.
description: Subscription-based service delivering local farm produce bags; members can choose home delivery or pickup at various locations around Oʻahu.
source_label: Oahu Fresh own shop site (undated); oahufresh.com Umeke ʻAi Pono page
notes: Delivery subscription, not a market, so no directory kind fits and kind is null. Own shop home page says delivery or pickup at various locations, but it is undated and I found no 2026 post, so still_active is null. The company's own site lists 916 Kaaahi Place, Honolulu 96817, (808) 476-7550 as its address (Oahu Food Hub); not used as a venue or address because it is not a public market site. Its Umeke ʻAi Pono community pickup program (Kaʻaʻawa, Wahiawa, Waipahu, Hauʻula, Kāneʻohe) ran only through July 4, 2025 and should not be listed. Old press: Star-Advertiser 2020 gave a $15 membership; Sierra Club 2020 gave a $20 farmers market bag. Current prices and delivery regions not re-verified. The @oahufresh handle comes from an Instagram post embedded in a 2020 Honolulu Magazine article, not from the own site. Facebook not captured.

name: OK Poultry (farm egg sales)
schedule_text: <cite index="32-14">Per an Onolicious Hawaiʻi post, the farm is only open Wednesday and Saturday.</cite> <cite index="36-12">A farm directory lists 7:30am to 1pm on those days.</cite> <cite index="32-13">The blog says to arrive before about 8:30am because eggs sell out.</cite> Not confirmed by a current first-party source.
description: <cite index="30-17,30-18">Eggs are bought directly at the farm; look for the OK Poultry sign on Kakaina Street.</cite> <cite index="33-5">Honolulu Magazine (older) describes a rustic shop with antiques and bins of produce from Waimānalo farmers.</cite>
source_label: Onolicious Hawaiʻi food blog (about 2 years old); localmeatmilkeggs.org directory; Honolulu Magazine (older)
notes: <cite index="30-26">The Onolicious OK Poultry post lists the address, phone 808-259-7832 and instagram.com/okpoultry.</cite> The Instagram URL is built from that blog's handle and was not checked on the platform itself. <cite index="36-10,36-11,36-12">The directory localmeatmilkeggs.org lists the same address and phone, open 7:30 am to 1 pm on Wednesday and Saturday.</cite> <cite index="33-4">Honolulu Magazine confirms the KK Poultry to OK Poultry ownership change.</cite> <cite index="31-2">A Nextdoor business page lists K K Poultry Farm Inc, same phone, with OK Poultry/Waimana TKG as its retail brand.</cite> A directory lists okpoultry.com but I could not verify it, so website is null. Old price ($15 per tray of 30 medium white eggs) was not used. No current first-party page or dated 2026 post was found, so still_active is null. Yelp was not used. Waimānalo is windward and borderline for an 'east' label.

name: Red Barn Farmstand
schedule_text: A Hawaii Life guide lists Wednesday through Sunday, 8:00am to 3:00pm, but this is likely outdated and the stand appears to be closed.
organizer: Holoholo General Store / Twin Bridge Farms partnership (original operators)
description: Opened in 2016 as an outdoor farmstand and café at Kamehameha Hwy and Cane Haul Rd in Haleiwa, selling local produce and prepared food.
source_label: Hawaii Mom Blog (community article); Hawaii Life guide for the old hours
notes: A December 2018 Hawaii Mom Blog post says Farm to Barn Cafe opened at the site of the former Red Barn Farmstand, which suggests Red Barn ended years ago. Aggregator listings (MapQuest, Wanderlog) also mark it permanently closed. The Hawaii Life guide's Wed–Sun 8am–3pm hours match older 2017 coverage and may be copied forward. I could not open redbarnfarmstand.com. The address 66-320 Kamehameha Hwy is also the address on Thrive Hawaii Family Farm's own site and Facebook page, so Thrive may now use or share that location; I did not confirm this. Phone per the Hawaii Life guide: (808) 753-4350. Recommend excluding unless a first-party source shows it is open.

name: Sun Farm Hawaii (farm produce)
schedule_text: The farm's website lists Monday through Friday, 8:30 AM to 12 PM as its contact hours. It does not say these are produce-sales hours.
organizer: Marcos and Michele Santos (Sun Farm Hawaii)
description: Family farm in Hawaii Kai growing fruit, vegetables and herbs. A KHON2 report said visitors can stop by the farm to buy locally grown fruit and veggies. The farm also runs garden tours.

Confirm directly that walk-up produce sales are still offered and when. The KHON2 piece also said they sell at local farmers markets.

name: Thrive Family Farm / Thrive Ohana Farm CSA
schedule_text: CSA runs in successive eight-week subscriptions (per Slow Food Oahu; undated). Organic produce was listed at $40/week. The farm's own events page lists 2025 CSA sign-ups and says to call 808-489-8305. A 2026 sign-up was not found.
organizer: Thrive Hawaii Family Farm (Jennifer and Jason Witte)
admission: Per Slow Food Oahu: organic produce $40/week.
description: Small organic family farm in Haleiwa selling vegetables through a member-supported CSA and to North Shore restaurants.
source_label: Organizer's own website and events page; Slow Food Oahu for the eight-week term
notes: Website, handle and Facebook can now be tied to this farm. thriveohana.org names Jason and Jennifer Witte, shows the Haleiwa address, and its events page lists the same phone, 808-489-8305, as Slow Food. The Facebook page for Thrive Hawaii Family Farm shows the same address and phone, and a Merry Christmas 2025 post. The Instagram profile @thrive.hawaii is titled Thrive Hawaii Family Farm, and the Roots Kalihi Valley hub-partner list gives the same handle. I did not see the site's own link text, so the handle rests on the profile name plus the Roots listing. Roots gives thriveohana.com for 'Thrive Ohana Farm', which looks like the same business, but I used thriveohana.org because Slow Food and the farm's own pages use it. The website pages are undated (about 2024–25), and I found no 2026 CSA sign-up, so whether the CSA is currently taking members is unconfirmed. The CSA pickup location is not stated. The address is the farm's listed address, not a confirmed pickup point. The same address is also listed for the former Red Barn Farmstand. Kind is left null because CSA is not in the allowed kinds. Eight-week terms and the $40/week price come from Slow Food only.

name: Waiahole Farm
description: <cite index="44-4">A TikTok discover page (updated 2026-10-26) describes Waiahole Farm as offering fresh-cut fruit, juices and seasonal tropical fruit on the Windward side.</cite>
source_label: TikTok discover page (aggregated social mention, not the business's own account)

Waiahole Nursery & Garden Center (own site waiaholenursery.com, 48-190 Kamehameha Hwy) and Waiahole Poi Factory are separate businesses. Needs a first-party source before it goes in the directory. still_active is null.

name: Waialua Fresh Egg Farm (farm stand)
venue_name: Waialua Fresh Egg Farm (listed in Honolulu Magazine as Villa Rose Egg Farm)
schedule_text: Sources disagree and the farm's own site was not retrieved. <cite index="56-5">Honolulu Magazine (March 2025 update) lists Friday to Sunday, 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.</cite> <cite index="54-4">A shopper's TikTok post (page updated 2026-09-21) says Thursday to Sunday, 8AM-5PM.</cite> <cite index="57-1,57-3">A Haleiwa Town guide says it is usually open until eggs sell out.</cite> Confirm hours with the farm.
description: <cite index="57-15,57-16">Sells fresh cage-free eggs straight from the farm at 65-1001 Kaukonahua Rd, Waialua.</cite> Sells eggs, not fruit.
source_label: Honolulu Magazine, 'Where to Buy Local Farm-Fresh Eggs on Oʻahu' (March 2025 update); Haleiwa Town guide; TikTok shopper post (Sept 2026)
notes: Address confirmed by Honolulu Magazine and the Haleiwa Town guide. Hours conflict as shown above, and no own page with stand hours was retrieved. Review and map listings were excluded, including the phone number found only there. The farm is operating: WATTAgNet (about Aug 2025) reported four new barns under construction, and Civil Beat (2023) reported an active farm. <cite index="54-4">A September 2026 TikTok post from a shopper who picked up eggs there</cite> supports the stand being open, so still_active is true. This is a recent third-party sign, not an owner confirmation, and confidence is medium. The farm is jointly owned by Hidden Villa Ranch and Rose Acre Farms (Civil Beat). <cite index="57-12,57-13">The Haleiwa Town guide also lists a separate 'Waialua Fresh' produce and pantry stand at 67-071 Nauahi St, Waialua, open daily 9 AM to 6 PM.</cite> I did not tie it to this egg stand and did not merge it. A shopper-reported price was not recorded as admission.

name: Waihuena Farm CSA
address: 59-414 Kamehameha Hwy, Haleiwa, HI 96712 (across from Pipeline)
schedule_text: The farm's homepage lists a roadside farmstand on Tuesdays, 12–6. Its 'Our Farmily' page says the Tuesday 12–6 farmstand and classes, and Wednesday 9–12 garden volunteer day, are by appointment only. A LocalHarvest listing (updated Jan 2025) says CSA members pick up shares at the farm fridge on Mon and Tue.
description: Organically managed North Shore farm offering a CSA program and a herdshare. Products are offered through membership rather than direct sale.
source_label: Organizer's own website (homepage and 'Our Farmily' page, undated)
notes: The farm's own pages are now confirmed: waihuenafarm.com gives the address, phone (808) 551-8132 and email info@waihuenafarm.com. The homepage says the farm is not yet permitted for sales and offers products through a herdshare and CSA membership, so products are 'not for sale' in the usual sense. The homepage says the roadside farmstand is open Tuesdays 12–6. The 'Our Farmily' page says it is by appointment only. Confirm with the farm before listing it as a walk-up stand. LocalHarvest (third-party, updated Jan 21, 2025) lists a $25 weekly CSA share, 20 shares, and pickup at the farm fridge. The farm's own site does not state a price. Instagram and email shown in the Sierra Club list could not be recovered, so the handle stays null rather than guessed. The own pages are undated, so I could not confirm the current state.

name: Mahiku Farmers Market
description: <cite index="24-1,24-2">A 2019 directory entry describes a year-round open-air market of local farmers, growers, artisans and food purveyors.</cite> That listing is dated and unverified.

Weekday hours on aggregator pages appear to come from map listings, so they were not used. <cite index="24-3">The October 2019 directory entry also listed Hyatt Regency Waikīkī (Tue/Thu) and Mililani (Fri) locations.</cite> Those are old and unverified. <cite index="25-6">vendorsmap.com lists the market as seasonal, contact organizer for schedule.</cite> Marketspread asks whether the market is still operational. No evidence it is active in 2026, so still_active is null. Verify with the organizer before publishing. Waimānalo is windward Oʻahu and borderline for an 'east' label.

name: Waimanalo Beach Park People's Open Market
schedule_text: Thursdays, 7:15 am to 8:15 am, year round (per aggregator listings). A 2018 state schedule says People's Open Markets close on all City holidays.
organizer: City and County of Honolulu Department of Parks and Recreation (People's Open Market program)
description: City-run weekly open market started to help farmers sell off-grade and surplus produce and to lower food costs. Sells produce and other food items. Accepts EBT/SNAP per the Revitalize Oʻahu directory. On Kalanianaʻole Highway near the baseball fields, with some parking and street parking.
source_label: Revitalize Oʻahu Oʻahu Farmers' Markets Directory (names C&C Parks and Recreation as host)
notes: Hours corrected to 7:15-8:15 am. This matches the Revitalize Oʻahu directory, a Generations808 schedule, an AARP event listing (Dec 2025 dates) and Soko. The 7:00-8:00 am hours come from an aggregator record dated to the 2015 season and are likely stale. I did not retrieve the City's own People's Open Market page, so there is no current own-page confirmation. Revitalize Oʻahu is a third-party directory, so confidence stays medium. The organizer is named only through that directory and the City's vendor rules PDF. The 2018 state schedule PDF is old. AARP dates are all 2025, so no 2026 dates are stated. Likely still running, but not confirmed by a current City source. Confirm with the City Parks and Recreation People's Open Market Unit.

name: Waimānalo Farmers Market

name: Aloha Festivals

schedule_text: Annual September celebration of Hawaiian culture. The 2026 (80th anniversary) Oʻahu events were: opening ceremony September 5, 4–6pm; the 72nd Waikīkī Hoʻolauleʻa September 19, 6–10pm (vendors from 4pm); and the 78th Floral Parade September 26 at 9am.

Vineyard Blvd (HNN 2026-02-23 and KHON2). Same organizer, different venue and name, so likely the same series. The Instagram handle @pacificexpohawaii comes from the KHON2 event listing and was not seen on the organizer's own page. Organizer phone given by KHON2 for the 2026 event: 808-732-6037. Side 'town' is my placement of Salt Lake in the urban Honolulu area. 2027 admission not stated.

source_label: Organizer website, with Hawaii News Now (April 26, 2026) for the 2026 details

name: Lei Day at Kapiʻolani Park

The Waimea Valley May Day event is separate and was not researched.

name: Okinawan FEASTival
venue_name: Okinawan-owned restaurants and food businesses across Oʻahu
schedule_text: Annual two-week run of restaurant specials after the Okinawan Festival. The 7th FEASTival ran September 7-21, 2026 (continuous range). The 2027 run has not been announced.
description: Two weeks of Okinawan-inspired specials at participating Okinawan-owned and Okinawan-at-heart restaurants and food businesses on Oʻahu, following the Okinawan Festival weekend.

I could not verify the conflicting 'November 2 - 8' line, so it is treated as a leftover. Okinawan Festival itself was Sept 5-6, 2026 at the Hawaii Convention Center (organizer). The Facebook page is the Okinawan Festival's own page, which also announces the FEASTival. still_active is true because the organizer ran the 2026 program and the series is annual.

name: Okinawan Festival
schedule_text: Annual festival around Labor Day weekend, run by the Hawaiʻi United Okinawa Association. The 44th edition was held September 5–6, 2026. Check okinawanfestival.com for the 2027 dates.

name: Punahou Carnival 2027: Party Like It's 2000
schedule_text: Two days, Friday February 5 and Saturday February 6, 2027, 11 AM-10 PM.
description: Punahou's annual financial-aid fundraiser carnival with food booths (including the famous malasadas), a large art gallery of Hawaiʻi artists, rides, games, a silent auction and live music.
source_label: Punahou School carnival page; Punahou Bulletin (Oct 20, 2026) confirms Feb 5-6 dates
notes: Food booths are school-run rather than independent vendors, but the carnival has a large art gallery of Hawaiʻi artists. Admission to the 2026 carnival was reported free (KITV); 2027 admission not stated. The Instagram handle comes from a Honolulu Magazine guide to the 2026 carnival.

name: Taste of Korea in Honolulu
schedule_text: One-day event held Saturday, May 16, 2026, 10am–3pm. The organizer's 2025 edition was Saturday, November 8, 2025 at Palama Settlement. No later edition has been found, so a repeat is unconfirmed.
description: Free-to-attend-style Korean cultural festival with K-food, hanbok, crafts and traditional games for families, per the organizer's Eventbrite page.
source_label: Organizer's Eventbrite event page
notes: The organizer's own Eventbrite listing shows the event has ended. It lists free parking on campus. The page does not state an admission price. The organizer's 2025 listing described the festival as free and family-friendly, but that does not confirm the 2026 price, so admission is left null. The street address is not stated in the sources, so I left it null. The 'side' is town because the listing says Honolulu; the neighborhood was not stated. A separate event with a similar name, also called Taste of Korea, is run by the Hawaiʻi Korean Cultural Center at Honolulu Country Club. Its 10th annual edition is on Nov 20 and tickets are $100 per KHON, so it is a different event and organizer. Do not merge them. An organizer website was not found. The event is over and the date has passed. Keep only if you want the one-time listing or a later edition is found.

name: The East Honolulu Food Festival
venue_name: Mary, Star of the Sea Church and Schools
schedule_text: Annual, held on a Saturday in early May, 5:30pm–9:30pm. The 18th annual edition was Saturday, May 2, 2026. The 2027 date is not confirmed; a third-party calendar lists May 2027 as TBC.
organizer: Mary, Star of the Sea Church and Schools
admission: Ticketed, all-inclusive tasting ticket. The 2026 price is not stated in the sources I opened.
description: Annual food festival with unlimited tastings from 20+ restaurants and purveyors, a silent auction, keiki activities and live DJ entertainment. The 2026 theme was 'Under the Moon in Old Hawaiʻi'. Free parking and shuttle from Kalani High School.
source_label: Hawaii News Now (news), cross-checked with Aloha State Daily and Hawaii Mom Blog
notes: The organizer, venue and 2026 date are now confirmed by several news and community articles from April 2026. I did not find an organizer website or social page, so confidence stays at medium. The Waikiki Beach Stays calendar still lists it under May 2027 with no date. The 2024 edition (16th) was ticketed at $95 for adults and $35 for keiki per KHON. I did not find the 2026 price. Chalk 2027 up as expected but unconfirmed.

name: Waikīkī SPAM JAM
schedule_text: Annual block party. The 2027 date is Saturday, April 24, 4:00–10:00pm. Participating restaurants run a Dine-In SPAM event April 17–May 2, 2027.
description: Food festival built around Spam dishes such as nachos, manapua and gelato. The 2026 edition had more than 40 food and retail booths. It is a fundraiser for the Hawaiʻi Foodbank, with donation tents on site.
source_label: Organizer website
notes: The source page does not give the street or venue for the block party.

name: We Are Samoa Festival
schedule_text: Annual festival. The 2027 edition runs April 21-29, 2027. It includes the World Fireknife Championships and the We Are Samoa High School Arts Festival (Saturday April 24, 2027). Men's finals are Thursday April 29 at 7:30 pm during the evening show Hā: Breath of Life.
admission: Ticketed. 2027 prices not found. In 2026, daytime competition sessions were $15 for all ages and the men's finals started at $94.95. The High School Arts Festival sold out in 2026 and was livestreamed on PCC's Facebook page.
description: Hawaiʻi's largest Samoan cultural festival, centered on the World Fireknife Championships and a high school Samoan arts festival at the Polynesian Cultural Center. Sessions: 2027-04-21 junior and intermediate preliminaries (9:30 am) and competition (6:30 pm); 2027-04-24 High School Arts Festival (9:00 am); 2027-04-28 men's qualifying (9:30 am) and men's preliminaries with the women's competition (6:30 pm); 2027-04-29 men's finals (7:30 pm).
source_label: Organizer website, World Fireknife Championships / We Are Samoa Festival (Polynesian Cultural Center)
notes: The organizer's page shows the 2027 dates and session times. Hawaii News Now (2026-05-04) names PCC as host of the 2026 edition. Dates match the third-party calendar. This is a ticketed cultural and competition event. No food or craft vendors are mentioned, so it may not suit a vendor directory. The organizer's social handles appear only in third-party aggregator markup, and the two Facebook URL variants differ, so I left them null. The page snapshot date is not shown, so source_date is null.

name: East Side Underground Market
schedule_text: Typically the first Saturday of every month, 4 to 9 p.m. (per Honolulu Magazine).
admission: Free
description: Monthly evening market listed among O‘ahu's vintage shopping events.
source_label: Honolulu Magazine, 'Where to Shop Vintage on Oʻahu This Summer' (2026)
notes: Third-party listing. Whether it continues past summer 2026 is unconfirmed. Not the same as Koko Marina Makers Market, which is already in the directory. Kind chosen as flea_market because the source groups it with vintage markets.

name: Free Parking Flea Market
venue_name: The Barn at SALT at Our Kakaʻako
schedule_text: Evening flea market on select dates. The summer 2026 edition was listed as August, date TBD, 5 to 10 p.m.
admission: Free
description: Evening flea market of vintage vendors and local small businesses, with local food vendors and live DJ sets.
source_label: Honolulu Magazine, 'Where to Shop Vintage on Oʻahu This Summer' (2026)
notes: No exact 2026 date was stated in the source. SALT's event pages I found were for 2025 editions. Check @freeparkingfleamarket for the next date. Separate from Makia Market, which is already in the directory.

name: Harbors Vintage Market
schedule_text: Periodic Saturday vintage markets from 3 to 7 p.m. 2026 dates listed: August 15 and September 12.
admission: Free
description: The two-story vintage shop becomes a market with vintage vendors and local businesses, selling clothing, accessories and collectibles.
source_label: Honolulu Magazine, 'Where to Shop Vintage on Oʻahu This Summer' (2026)
notes: Third-party listing; I did not verify against the organizer's own page. Both dates have already passed. Check the shop's site or Instagram for later dates.

name: Wiki Wiki One Day Vintage Collectibles & Hawaiiana Show
venue_name: Neal S. Blaisdell Center (Galleria and Hawaiʻi Suites)
schedule_text: A few one-day shows per year, usually on a Sunday. Regular shopping hours 11 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. 2026 dates: March 22, July 19, October 4, November 22.
admission: $6 general admission; free for two kids 12 and under with each paid adult ticket
description: Vintage collectibles and Hawaiiana show with 100+ vendor tables. Vendors come from the outer islands, Oʻahu, Japan and the U.S. mainland.
source_label: Organizer Instagram bio (2026 dates), corroborated by Aloha State Daily 2026-09-21 and Blaisdell Center events calendar
notes: Mar 22 and Oct 4 times come from the Blaisdell Center listing. Nov 22 times assume the 'regular shopping hours' stated in the Aloha State Daily article. The July 19 time was not confirmed (a third-party listing showed a different window), so it is null. Early entry was 10:00 a.m. for the Mar 22 and Oct 4 shows. Oct 4 has already happened.

name: Mele Market at Pearl at Kalauao
schedule_text: Pearl at Kalauao's homepage lists its monthly night market for Wednesday, December 9, 5pm–9pm, billed as the end-of-2026 market. The regular schedule on the night-markets page is the last Wednesday of each month, 5pm–9pm. Dec 9 is not the last Wednesday, so the December date differs from the usual pattern.
admission: Free admission (parking also free per earlier 2026 listings)
description: Monthly evening night market at the golf-course venue with 100+ local vendors, live entertainment, food, desserts and shopping, per the organizer's homepage.
source_label: Organizer's own website (homepage, seen 2026-10-31)
notes: Kind corrected from holiday_fair to night_market. The name 'Mele Market' appears only on the third-party calendar. No Pearl page uses it. This is almost certainly the December edition of the Last Wednesdays Night Market, so treat it as a duplicate and merge. The 2025 December edition was branded 'Holiday Night Market' (KSBE alumni calendar, Dec 10, 2025). The organizer page does not list vendor types beyond food, desserts and shopping. The night-market Instagram named in Honolulu Magazine is @nightmarketcentral. Pearl's own events page points to @pearlatkalauao. source_date is null because the page is undated. Dec 9 is unusual for a 'last Wednesday' market, so recheck the date before publishing. Side 'central' follows a third-party grouping of this market under Central Oʻahu and Pearl Harbor; ʻAiea could also be read as leeward_ewa.

name: Annual Unthirsty Plant Sale (Hālawa Xeriscape Garden)
schedule_text: Annual sale, typically early August. The 2026 sale was Saturday Aug 1, 9am-1pm. The 2027 date has not been announced in the sources found.
organizer: Honolulu Board of Water Supply, co-sponsored by Friends of Hālawa Xeriscape Garden
admission: Free admission; free street parking and a shuttle on Iwaena Street. Payments by major credit card only (no cash).
description: Drought-tolerant and native plants from local vendors, with agency and community booths, mini-workshops, a rain barrel giveaway, a Cactus & Succulent Society of Hawaiʻi display, and a UH Master Gardener Plant Doctors booth.
source_label: Honolulu Board of Water Supply (organizer page)
notes: This event has already happened. The Honolulu Orchid Society also staffed an orchid-care booth, per a KHON story dated 2026-07-25. The central side tag is my reading of the Hālawa location, and the source does not give a city or ZIP. The Friends of Hālawa Xeriscape Garden offer a membership with 10% off plant purchases.

name: Ewa Orchid Society Orchid Show and Plant Sale
schedule_text: Annual show. The 2026 show (76th annual) was Friday July 17 and Saturday July 18, 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM. The 2027 date has not been announced in the sources found.
description: 76th annual orchid show and plant sale with the theme 'Christmas in July' (Honolulu Orchid Society listing). Judging was held the evening of July 16.
source_label: American Orchid Society event calendar, corroborated by the Honolulu Orchid Society event listing
notes: This event has already happened. Venue, address and times come from the American Orchid Society calendar; the Honolulu Orchid Society listing gives July 17 9:00 am to July 18 4:00 pm and names the Ewa Elementary School Cafeteria. Per-day 9-4 hours follow the AOS show times, so verify. Both sources are third-party; the Ewa Orchid Society's own site or social page was not found, so confidence stays medium. Admission not stated. The 2027 date has not been announced in the sources found. still_active is true because the society held its 76th annual show in July 2026.

name: Honolulu Orchid Society Orchid Show & Plant Sale (87th Annual, "Orchids Spooktacular")
schedule_text: Annual show, held on a Friday and Saturday in October. The 2026 show was Oct 9-10, 9am-4pm both days. The plant sale closed at 3pm on Saturday. The 2027 date has not been announced in the sources found.
admission: Free admission and parking
description: Orchid displays by the Honolulu Orchid Society and guest societies, a plant sale by island nurseries, a country store, free orchid workshops, a plant doctor, and UH CTAHR and HDOA information tables.
source_label: Honolulu Orchid Society (organizer page)
notes: This event has already happened as of 2026-10-31. Other sources: AOS calendar says no AOS judging; Hoodline article dated 2026-10-05. Plant sale hours are 9-4 Friday and 9-3 Saturday. Neighborhood not stated in the sources.

name: Kunia Orchid Society 68th Orchid Show & Plant Sale
schedule_text: Two-day annual show. The 2026 show ran Friday March 20 and Saturday March 21, theme "March Madness". The 2027 date has not been announced in the sources found.
admission: Free
description: Orchid show and plant sale held in the Leilehua High School gym by the Kunia Orchid Society.
source_label: Honolulu Orchid Society events calendar (listing for a sister society's show)
notes: This event has already happened. The 9am-5pm time is the one the listing shows for March 20. Saturday hours were not stated. Kunia Orchid Society is also listed as a guest society on the HOS show page. Check the Kunia Orchid Society's own page for the 2027 date.

name: Lyon Arboretum Fall Plant & Craft Sale
venue_name: Harold L. Lyon Arboretum (surrounding the Visitor Center and Greenhouse)
schedule_text: Friday Dec 4 and Saturday Dec 5, 2026, 9 AM to 3 PM each day
organizer: Harold L. Lyon Arboretum, University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa
description: Fall plant and craft sale at Lyon Arboretum in Mānoa Valley with local vendors, music and food. Plants include tropical ornamentals, Hoya, natives, ferns, orchids, jade vines, aroids, gingers, bromeliads and carnivorous plants from Lyon's Horticulture Dept., Hui Ku Maoli Ola, Laʻau Hawaiʻi, Olomana Tropicals, Lang's Nursery, Mix Plate Nurseries, Nuʻuanu Orchids and others. Also aloha shirts, local honey and art. Proceeds support Lyon Arboretum's conservation, education and research.
source_label: Lyon Arboretum (organizer) event page
notes: Page indicates a vehicle-based parking reservation system (one reservation per vehicle). Reservation booking date and admission price were cut off in the retrieved text, so verify on the organizer page. Street address not stated in the source.

venue_name: Harold L. Lyon Arboretum (around the Visitor Center and greenhouse)
schedule_text: Annual spring sale in May. The 2026 sale was Friday May 8 and Saturday May 9, 9am to 3pm each day. Walk-ups without reservations were admitted from 10:30am.
organizer: Harold L. Lyon Arboretum, University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa
description: Spring plant and craft sale with tropical ornamentals, native plants, orchids, begonias, hoyas, ferns and exotic edibles, plus handmade goods.
source_label: Hawaiʻi Public Radio community calendar (Lyon Arboretum listing)
notes: This event has already happened. Parking reservations were via Eventbrite, opening April 13, 2026. A 2027 date has not been announced in the sources found.

description: Weekly plant sale at the Waimea Valley Nursery with a variety of plants for home and garden, including fruiting and flowering plants, native trees and easy-care greenery.

description: Annual orchid show and plant sale run by the Windward Orchid Society in the S.W. King Intermediate cafeteria.

name: Kailua Swap Meet
schedule_text: Irregular 'Kailua Mini Swap' garage-sale events on Saturdays, about every few months. 2026 dates found: Feb 21, Aug 1 and Oct 17. Next date not found.
description: Community garage-sale 'mini swap' held with Emmanuel Church Kailua. The Feb 2026 booth page says 30+ stalls for families decluttering, and the church's Facebook page says 32 community-operated booths for the Aug 1 edition. Booths are split between the Emmanuel lot and the adjacent Cole Academy lot.
source_label: Organizer ticketing page (Ticket Tailor); Emmanuel Episcopal Church events page
notes: Dates come from the organizer's Ticket Tailor listings (Feb 21 and Oct 17, 2026) and the church's own events page (Aug 1, 2026). KITV also ran Feb 21. The Facebook post '6/6' (no year shown) is consistent with a Saturday in 2026, but I did not list it as a date. Address 780 Keolu Dr is from the church's own Facebook page. The swap meet's Facebook intro lists 281 Ilihau St, which I did not use. The $25 garage-sale booth fee was stated for Feb 2026 and Mar 2025 listings; shopper admission is not stated. The Oct 17 date has already passed, so check the organizer page for the next edition.
